text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 30 people are feared dead and scores are injured in a horrific road accident on the Nairobi-Nakuru highway.
- Police deny there was a death in an aborted opposition rally in Nairobi over the weekend.
- A man is stoned to death in a confrontation between rival groups in a parish in western Kenya.
- A confrontation between Kenyan opposition leaders and security personnel over the weekend draws mixed reactions from leaders.
- The revamped opposition National Democratic Party of Kenya appears headed for a split following a clash between chairman Stephen Oludhe and member Raila Odinga.
- Scores of families flee Marakwet district in the rift valley, fearing cattle rustlers from a neighbouring district.
- An attempted robbery on a mining company in Voi near Kenya's coast is foiled.
- The executive director of the U.N. Centre for Human Settlement responds to criticism by releasing a revitalisation plan for the centre.
- A total of 20,600 tonnes of Brazilian sugar said to be in transit is expected to arrive today at the Mombasa port.
- The removal of Kenya Railways executive chairman Jeremiah Musuva comes barely three weeks after he defended performance of the cash-strapped parastatal.
- Burundi leader Pierre Buyoya sends a delegation to meet Tanzanian leader Benjamin Mkapa to discuss border tension.

- Human rights, good governance, transparency and democracy could be among the criteria demanded by the East African Cooperation from countries wishing to join the regional body. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
